Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: A friend who has just started assembling furniture asks for a quick video call because the instructions are confusing.
Expectation2: Adhere to site protocols and work effectively as part of the team.
Situation2: The mandatory daily pre-work safety briefing is starting in two minutes.
Story:
My phone buzzed in my pocket just as I was grabbing my hard hat. It was Sam, my oldest friend, his message popping up: “Can you hop on a quick video call? I’m lost with this furniture and the instructions make no sense.” I could almost hear the frustration in his words. I knew he’d just moved in and was probably surrounded by half-built shelves and scattered screws. Helping him out was what friends did, especially when things got tough.

But at the same time, the foreman’s voice echoed across the site, calling everyone to the daily safety briefing. Missing it wasn’t an option—site rules were strict, and the team counted on everyone being present and focused. If I skipped it, I’d be letting my crew down and risking a write-up, maybe even suspension.

I stared at my phone, thumb hovering over the call button, heart pounding. Sam needed me, but so did my team. The seconds ticked by, and I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in, each demanding something I wasn’t sure I could give.
